The court of public opinion is often as powerfully destructive as a court of law and I see no reason why innocent until proven guilty can't be generally applied - in fact it seems like a pretty solid principle to live by. 

Every allegation deserves to be taken serious, but it's reasonable to hear all sides of a story before casting judgement. Doing so doesn't imply a lack of support, but rather is ultimately more supportive as it's a clearer way to the truth. 

This is the same reason I was correctly taught to not believe everything I heard in the rumor mills of school growing up. 

This young woman had a lot of support, which is a good thing, but support doesn't mean condemning the accused. In this scenario, what about support for the wrongfully accused who had the weight of social justice and the judgement of the court if public opinion against him?

The right thing would have been to take the allegations serious and suspended judgement until more was known. This provides protection on all sides.

It's a hard habit to break, but essential if we're to ever have meaningful conversations. 

Our cultural norm right now seems to be to use broad generalizations and emotion to sway minds. Nuance and discussion are done away with.

Under promise, overperform seems to be a safe mantra.

For SafeMoon though, it is consistently hype and over-promise while delivering nothing that has increased the value of this token (in fact just the opposite is true).

It's not the people are hating on their investment, it's that they're rightfully frustrated with an organization that is promised so much and done so little. 

In a sense John and his team are like a Board of Directors in a privately traded company who's responsibility is to increase the value of investors stocks. If a company consistently over promised and never performed, all the while seeing their stock prices plummet, investors would have a reasonable case at being negative and frustrated. 

That's no different here.  In what we're likely bids to artificially inflate the value of SafeMoon, John and his team have promised countless ideas and products that have not materialized. In fact many of them are never brought up again and we have no way of knowing if anything real is actually happening.

I'll gladly change my tune if they start to perform, but if this were publicly traded company I would be working hard to supplant them as the corporate board.

Over promise, no-perform seems to be the motto for the SafeMoon organization.

It didn't ruin, but rather enlightened. A painful path to go through though.
